refnamediv.refpurpose: Read and parse the request body and return the result

refentry.refsect1:
&reftitle.description;
arrayrequest_parse_body arraynulloptions&null;
This function reads the request body and parses it according to the Content-Type header. Currently, two content types are supported:
application/x-www-form-urlencoded
multipart/form-data
This function is used primarily to parse multipart/form-data requests with HTTP verbs other than POST which do not automatically populate the $_POST and $_FILES superglobals.
The request body can only be consumed once. request_parse_body consumes the request body without buffering it to the php://input stream. Conversely, if the body has already been read (e.g. via php://input), request_parse_body will return empty data.

&reftitle.parameters;
options
The options parameter accepts an associative array to override the following global &php.ini; settings for parsing of the request body.
max_file_uploads max_input_vars max_multipart_body_parts post_max_size upload_max_filesize
Keys are matched case-insensitively. Any key that is not given keeps the value of the &php.ini; directive of the same name. Each value is either an int, or a string using the shorthand notation, as in '10M'.

&reftitle.returnvalues;
request_parse_body returns an array pair with the equivalent of $_POST at index 0 and $_FILES at index 1.

&reftitle.errors;
A RequestParseBodyException is thrown when the request provides no Content-Type header, when that header names an unsupported content type, or when the body is invalid according to it.
A RequestParseBodyException is also thrown when one of the limits is exceeded, that is the number of file uploads, the number of input variables, the number of multipart body parts, or the body size, and when the boundary of a multipart/form-data body is missing or invalid. Outside of request_parse_body, the same conditions only raise an E_WARNING.
A ValueError is thrown when options contains invalid keys, or invalid values for the corresponding key.
An E_WARNING is raised, rather than an exception being thrown, when a value given in the shorthand notation cannot be parsed; the degraded value is used and parsing continues. On application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies, exceeding post_max_size also raises an E_WARNING and yields an empty result instead of throwing.
